question.text: The velocity and acceleration vectors of a particle undergoing circular motion are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>v</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mtext>i</mtext><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>a</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mtext>i</mtext><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mover><mtext>j</mtext><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively at an instant of time. What is the radius (in <math><mtext>m</mtext></math>) of the circle?

solution.text:
It can be observed that the component of acceleration perpendicular to velocity is a=4 m s-2

∴   Radius=v2ac=224=1 m
